items.title: Richard Brunies Interview, 1959-04-27
items.q: Older's brother Henney come along, he picked it up. He learned it. Well, he's dead now.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. Yeah, yeah. You really learned by yourself, and you didn't have any lessons except a couple you learned.

And the reason the other boys learned, I went out and bought the instruments and I couldn't blow them like a trombone. Trombone? They were on the yard or laid on the table. Mm-hmm. Older's brother Henney come along, he picked it up. He learned it. Well, he's dead now.

Well, can you tell us a little bit about your brother, Henry, because he's not here, of course, to talk for us. Well, he was a hot friend. He was a wonderful, I've heard. Yes, he was. He was a showman with his son. I had that to say. How much younger was he than you? He was younger than you? Oh, yeah. Next to him. About five years. About five years. And, uh...
